# Orc and Goblin Nemeses

*Pages PDF 102-109*

## ## Orc and Goblin Nemeses
Orcs and Goblins can make classic nemeses for adventurers, and there are many Orc and Goblin chieftains in the Old World and beyond who can provide a challenge to a party across a wide territory. Not only are they fierce combatants and aggressive antagonists themselves, but their lieutenants and underlings act with a degree of loyalty provided they are well led and kept busy enough so that animosity doesn’t decimate the ranks. 

## **Predictable Foes?**
For the most part, Orcs and Goblins are simple antagonists. They are violently competitive with almost everything they encounter, possess an almost elemental degree of spite and hostility, and have such an appetite for conflict that they will engage in it even if it is clearly against their own best interest. 

It is fair to say that all Orcs and Goblins have a taste for supremacy, and are not subtle in their attempts to achieve it. However, Orcs and Goblins can be sly in their tactics, or driven to compromise through desperate circumstances. 

The Nemesis Traits table can be used by a GM to generate ideas for the behaviour of a particular Orc or Goblin leader. Whilst it reinforces the notion that typical Orcs and Goblins will seek to dominate their foes in a straightforward, brutal manner, it can show that there are other sides to their character, or at least that their brutality can come in a variety of flavours. 

Roll 1d10 on each of the three columns of the table to see what manner of behaviours and ambitions are peculiar to a particular Orc or Goblin chieftain. 

Traits may be used to confer the following abilities to an Orc or Goblin nemesis. A _Cunning_ Trait should provide him with an asset to be used. Achieving an important step towards an _Ambition_ Trait should provide a single level of the _Luck_ Talent. A satisfying application of his _Brutality_ Trait means his forces are immune to the effects of _Animosity_ for a week. 

## **Combined Traits**
Particularly successful or eccentric Orc and Goblin chieftains may possess a number of these traits, so a GM may decide to keep rolling for, or choosing traits, until they feel they have a suitably interesting foe to torment their players with. 

For example, the Night Goblin Warlord Skarsnik (page 104) is a complex character who prioritises his own security through strategy and fortification. This allows him to build the legacy he craves, which he does primarily through terrorising the Dwarfs of Karak Eight Peaks. He dominates a number of local tribes, and is more than prepared to use them as patsies if a suitable opportunity presents itself. 

- **Cunning:** Preferred Enemy (Dwarfs), Bodyguard (his Cave Squig Gobbla), Fortifier, Vassals, Council of Night Goblin Shamans, Scapegoats, and Sly. 

- **Brutality:** Sadistic, Besieger, and Horror. 

- **Ambition:** Consolidation, Alliance (with Gorfang Rotgut), and Legacy. 

Whereas Gorfang Rotgut (page 106) is rather more typical of an Orc Warlord. His appetite for violence and revenge against the Dwarfs is somewhat hampered by his habit of remaining within Black Crag for long stretches of time (though should Skarsnik exercise more influence in the area, he may develop an ambition for independence from the Night Goblin’s schemeing and sneaking). 

- **Cunning:** Preferred Enemy (Dwarfs), Fortifier. 

- **Brutality:** Sadistic, Besieger, and Horror. 

- **Ambition:** Complacency and Revenge.

## **Skarsnik**
Skarsnik is the notorious chieftain of the Crooked Moon tribe, the most powerful Night Goblin of the World’s Edge Mountains, the most successful Goblin Warlord since Grom the Paunch, and perhaps the wiliest Goblin to have lived. He takes great pride in his achievements. He leads his hordes from a black iron throne in the Hall of a Thousand Pillars at the heart of Karak Eight Peaks, flanked by a hundreds of Dwarf-tallow candles and tended by Shaman advisors in contact with his network of spies via smoke signal and drum. 

The ‘King in da Mountain’, Skarsnik is the undisputed leader of the Orcs and Goblins to the east of Death Pass. While some Orcs resist kowtowing to a Goblin, challengers invariably meet their demise. Skarsnik is fierce in battle, but never fights fairly. He is aided by Gobbla, the gigantic Cave Squig he keeps chained to his side. Gobbla exhibits deranged hostility towards everyone other than its master, and has grown fat and strong off the corpses of Skarsnik’s foes. 

Skarsnik spawned as the runt among his brethren. Smaller, weaker Goblins often fall victim to fatal bullying, or are killed by Skaven and Dwarfs lurking underground. Skarsnik thrived through spiteful resolve, disciplined patience, good fortune bordering on divine providence, and terrifying genius. He has since grown powerful and has become a brilliant tactician. 

Though none of his boyz can appreciate the depths of his genius, Skarsnik understands their limits, and is well-accustomed to forcing discipline on cowards and fools. Under his commands, dispersed through the least stupid of his minions, a Goblin horde becomes an army any commander would envy. His charisma inspires steadfast confidence, and when suicidal bravery is needed, intoxicating fungal brews provide the necessary courage. 

This level of control lets Skarsnik execute devious traps and ambushes. When King Belegar Ironhammer campaigned to recapture Karak Eight Peaks, Skarsnik forced his clan into avoidance and cautious observation. They watched as the Dwarfs rebuilt their citadel but refrained from frontal assault. Instead, Skarsnik coordinated the opportunistic capture of stragglers, and tortured his prisoners audibly near the citadel walls to bait rescuers. Resultant attrition has weakened Belegar’s forces so severely that they can no longer escape. 

Nearly forty years ago, Belegar successfully sent word of his predicament to Karaz-a-Karak, the Dwarf Capital. Duregar, Belegar’s kinsman, gathered a throng to free him. When they arrived, they found Skarsnik’s horde large enough to overwhelm them. Duregar led his people along the mountainsides to give the Crooked Moon a wide berth, hoping to quickly break through the eastern gate he understood to be less fortified. 

Skarsnik let Duregar advance towards the gate before encircling his forces and deploying archers and siege machines from half-ruined watchtowers nearby. Duregar’s throng was almost doomed, but Belegar sallied out from the citadel. The survivors escaped inside to join Belegar in his prison. 

Many years later, Belegar and Duregar remain trapped, their view from the citadel decorated with an evergrowing array of beard scalps torn from their people. For such cruelty, Skarsnik has earned his own chapter in the Great Book of Grudges. 

Skarsnik is also reviled by the Skaven, whom he has often out-manoeuvred and out-betrayed. He has had their flesh-stripped skulls fashioned into grim markers throughout his underground territory. These are meant to terrify the ratmen but have been taken for provocation. Queek Headtaker of Clan Mors leads his forces at the behest of Warlord Gnawdwell. Queek is murderously violent and uncommonly brave for a Skaven, and has vowed to add Skarsnik’s head to his trophy rack. 

Emboldened by his victories, Skarsnik has launched attacks against Karak Azul, Barak Varr, and throughout the Badlands. His influence grows and his ambitions have been stoked by an alliance with Gorfang Rotgut, who rules Iron Rock to the west of Death Pass.  Skarsnik distrusts the Orc, but envisions Gorfang ‘leading’ a massive Waaagh! from the front as he puppeteers it from the shadows. 

**GOBBLA, BLOATED CAVE SQUIG**

## Skarsnik’s Prodda
Skarsnik’s signature weapon is a polearm known as a prodda. These weapons are designed by Night Goblins to help them goad Squigs, and they count as Halberds. Skarsnik’s Prodda has been enchanted by his Shaman advisors to project the spite of Night Goblins. Attacks made with the prodda count as magical. Skarsnik may use it to cast the _Vindictive Glare_ spell (page 99). He may do this as an Action, and is treated as having Language (Magick) 75 for the purpose of casting the spell. Furthermore the spell benefits from +1 SL for every Night Goblin within WP Bonus yards (6 in Skarsnik’s case). 

## **Gorfang Rotgut**
Gorfang Rotgut is the massive, aggressive, and monstrously powerful chieftain of the Red Fangs tribe of Orcs. He is known as the ‘Troll-Eater’ due to his penchant for hunting the beasts with his mighty choppa, which he calls the Red Fang, and then consuming great steaks carved from their flesh. 

This habit swells his infamy as much as his gut, serving not only as proof of his great strength, but also conjuring memories of fat Grom, the Troll-bloated Goblin Warlord who once led a great Waaagh! across the Empire and to the shores of Ulthuan. 

Gorfang has led his tribe to dominate western Death Pass, where they have seized Black Crag (and the ruins of the Dwarf hold of Karak Drazh within) for their homeland. Karak Drazh was first conquered by Orcs in –649 IC, and the hold is a live-in trophy for the region’s biggest, loudest, and most violent Orc bosses. Gorfang is the latest of a long line of Orc chiefs who have occupied the ruined hold, and as the ‘King of Black Crag’, he imposes his will over the nearby tribes he has subjugated. 

Although all renowned Orcs invariably attract the hostility of the Dwarfs, Gorfang is among the most despised. His notorious and sustained occupancy of their ancestral halls has earned him many grudges under the title of the ‘Squatter King’. Numerous battles against Dwarfs and injuries at their hands have forged in Gorfang an earnest hatred for ‘stunties’ matched by a keen understanding of the threat they pose to his rule. 

Gorfang is clever for an Orc and recognizes the many factors bearing upon the balance of power in his domain. Because he is also very aggressive, by any standard, this recognition does nothing to deter his warmaking, or to pause growth of the deliberately outrageous collection of Dwarf beards he wears into battle. Instead, Gorfang’s savvy has led him to one of the rarest of skills among Warbosses: politicking. 

Caught between the looming threat of Dwarfen vengeance, the ever-lurking Skaven menace, and his insatiable desire to bully tolls from anyone passing through his territory, Gorfang has brokered an uneasy alliance with Skarsnik, Goblin leader of the Crooked Moon tribe and the other ‘King’ of Death Pass. Skarsnik has ruled the Night Goblins of eastern Death Pass for decades, and places a check on Gorfang’s ability to expand eastward. Sharing the territory frustrates Gorfang, who views Skarsnik with the same disdain he affords all ‘runts’. This instinctive distaste is outweighed not only by Skarsnik’s efficacy in battle, but also Gorfang’s grudging admiration for the creative sadism the Goblin inflicts upon Dwarfs whenever possible. 

The Greenskin alliance was forged in 2498 IC, after the Battle of the Jaws at Mad Dog Pass where the Red Fangs fought a force of Dwarf Rangers sent from Karaz-aKarak for the express purpose of slaying Gorfang. The ambush nearly broke the tribe, and Gorfang lost an eye in combat. As the Troll-Eater was wounded, and the Dwarfs surged to overwhelm their foes, Skarsnik and his Goblins sprung from hiding high on the pass. The Rangers’ gunnery teams were wiped out instantly, and a full charge hit the rear of their extended formation. This ambush closed the ‘Jaws’ on the Rangers, who, exhausted and surrounded, were eradicated. 

Whilst he is irked by the notion of regarding a mere Goblin as any sort of peer, Gorfang had been toying with the idea of allying with the Crooked Moon. He made a pact to cooperate with Skarsnik soon after the battle. Skarsnik, who had spent years whispering in the leathery ears of the Troll-Eater’s Goblin toadies, agreed. 

With Skarsnik’s support and a new iron eyepatch, Gorfang has pursued even more spectacular exploits. His siege of Barak Varr earned many new grudges, but was easily outdone by the Red Fangs’ assault on Karak Azul. 

While King Kazador was away hunting Goblins, Gorfang led his tribe into the hold through an ancient tunnel whose location had been lost in the Begrid clan’s records ages before. 

The Orcs of the Red Fang tribe stormed Karak Azul, defaced its Ancestral Statues, befouled the best of its ale stores, and captured at least fifty of Kazador’s kinfolk, including Morga, his queen. 

To Kazador’s great sorrow, these captives still languish in the dungeons of Black Crag. Kazrik, the Dwarf King’s son, was spared this fate. He was instead made a message of conquest: shaved, tattooed with a crude Orc glyph, and nailed to his father’s throne as a cruel ‘gift’. Though he survived, his mind has never truly recovered, and Kazrik is keenly aware that he is branded with a mark of the Orcish gods symbolising Gorfang’s ownership. Kazador has since spent many sleepless nights wondering who betrayed their hold by revealing the secret entrance to the Squatter King.

## The Red Fang
Gorfang’s signature choppa is a magical weapon, cruelly serrated and perfectly balanced for his arm. It has the following Qualities: _Damaging_ , _Fast_ , and grants the wielder the _Magical_ Creature Trait. 

## **Sog’kog**
Of the many monsters that haunt the frozen wilderness of the Troll Country, the great beast known as Sog’Kog has gained notoriety, both for his unthinking ferocity and grave depredations, but also because a story as to his origins and behaviour has become widely known. Each year, the Tsar of Kislev despatches a squadron of his finest knights, members of the Gryphon Legion, to Middenheim, and the Graf of that city reciprocates by sending a regiment of his loyal Knights Panther to serve the Tsar. 

The Ostland port of Salkalten is a stopping point on the journey, and locals there tell a tale of a great Troll that once haunted the Forest of Shadows, and how its fate was intertwined with a rogue Gold Wizard who had once served the court of Baron von Wolder. The mage, though trained and endorsed by the College of the Gold Order in Altdorf, became obsessed with the use of Warpstone, and fell to Chaos, becoming the self-styled Warlord Vorl, sorcerer of Tzeentch. 

Vorl erected a stone tower deep in the Forest of Shadows, where he could conduct his experiments. He gathered a retinue of Beastmen and other horrors to his side, among them the Common Troll Sog. Vorl thought the creature would be pliable to his enchantments, but Sog, like all Trolls, was unbiddable, particularly when hungry. 

One day, Sog smashed the tower’s thick wooden door from its iron hinges and devoured Vorl. The tower was full of strange contraptions, glass tubes stretched everywhere, connected to alembics, and bottles filled with bubbling liquids. Gold glittered in crucibles, along with lead-lined boxes of strange, green, glowing rocks. Sog quickly decided to claim the tower as his lair, making a nest from books and cast-off robes to sleep in before greedily consuming the contents of the various containers and vials without pause. 

That night, pain wracked Sog. His flesh bubbled, erupting into tendrils and mouths that consumed one another over and over. Through it all, Sog heard a voice growing louder and louder in his head, mimicking his thoughts as it fought its way to the surface. 

Sog, tormented by the agonies of his transformation, passed into unconsciousness, only waking the next day. He found a new head had burst from his chest, its eyes glittering with malign intelligence. It called itself Kog, a vile reflection of the most vicious and violent aspects of its host. This new head quickly gained dominance, giving rise to Sog’Kog, the Chaos Troll. 

The creature headed north, avoiding the major towns of Ostland and Kislev, but leaving a trail of destruction through the countryside. It now lurks within the Troll Country, but each winter, it preys upon the folk who inhabit the camps and villages of Kislev’s northern border. 

Sog’Kog is vicious and unthinking, but the malign powers of Chaos that flow through his system have affected his behaviour. He satisfies his hunger by stealing cattle or raiding villages, but when he isn’t starving, he likes to stalk his prey, following at a distance, lurking on the horizon, relishing in the anxiety his monstrous form inspires. 

Sog’Kog’s great delight is to stalk a group of travellers through the wilderness, haunting their steps and appearing for a brief moment on the horizon, or at the edge of woodland, and then vanishing just as soon as he is percieved. It is only when his quarry glimpse the sight of a town that promises sanctuary that Sog’Kog falls upon them to rend them limb from limb and sate his horrible hunger. He always leaves a sole survivor to spread the tale of the horror they have witnessed.
